Choose one —
• Destroy target creature with flying.

Enchant creature
Whenever enchanted creature deals damage to an opponent, you may draw a card.

Whenever you cast a creature spell, create a 3/3 green Beast creature token.

annotations.description: Casting Wildwood Scourge for X=1 creates a fragile 1/1 that's vulnerable to almost any removal. While there's synergy with Trufflesnout next turn, the Scourge's value scales with X and with surviving to accumulate counters. A 1/1 is much easier to kill than a larger version cast later.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Wildwood Scourge for X=1, making a 1/1 Hydra
annotations.betterLine: Hold the Scourge and pass with 2 mana open. Next turn play Thriving Grove, cast Trufflesnout (choosing +1/+1 counter mode). On a later turn, cast Scourge for X=2+ when it's harder to remove and the board has more +1/+1 counter synergies established.

annotations.description: Casting Curiosity on the opponent's Wildwood Scourge gives the opponent card draw whenever their creature deals damage to QwCdr Folksy. This is actively harmful — it's enchanting an enemy creature with a beneficial aura. Curiosity triggers when the enchanted creature deals damage to an opponent, and from the Scourge's perspective, QwCdr Folksy is the opponent. So whenever the Scourge hits QwCdr Folksy, GPT53C Trash draws a card. This wastes a card and actively helps the opponent.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Curiosity targeting opponent's Wildwood Scourge
annotations.betterLine: Cast Narcolepsy on the opponent's Wildwood Scourge to lock it down, or simply pass and hold mana for Last Gasp as removal. Curiosity should only be cast on your own creatures.

annotations.description: Chose Armorcraft Judge (3/3, draws 1 card) over Fertilid when Primeval Bounty ({5}{G}) is in hand. Fertilid would ramp toward the game-winning 6-mana enchantment by fetching lands, potentially casting it 1-2 turns sooner. The single card draw from Armorcraft Judge doesn't compensate for the tempo loss of delaying Primeval Bounty.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Armorcraft Judge, drawing 1 card off Trufflesnout's counter
annotations.betterLine: Cast Fertilid ({2}{G}), leaving 1 mana open. Next turn activate Fertilid to fetch a land, reaching 5 lands. Then cast Primeval Bounty on turn 6 lands instead of having to wait longer without ramp.

annotations.description: At 11 life facing two 3/3 creatures with all lands untapped, the player passed their entire precombat main phase without casting any of three available spells. They had 3 mana available (UUB) and could cast Library Larcenist, Silversmote Ghoul, or Rousing Read. This wastes an entire turn of mana while significantly behind on board.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority in precombat main phase, casting nothing and effectively ending the turn.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Silversmote Ghoul (3/1 body that synergizes with Blood Artist's life gain for recursion and provides a meaningful blocker/attacker) or Library Larcenist (card draw engine). Either play develops the board when desperately behind at 11 life.

annotations.description: Silversmote Ghoul is a fragile 3/1 with a recursion ability that's unlikely to trigger (no reliable way to gain 3 life). Meanwhile, Rousing Read on Blood Artist would immediately draw 2 cards (discard 1), create a 1/2 flyer, and provide immediate card advantage at a critical low-life juncture where finding answers matters most.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Silversmote Ghoul, deploying a fragile 3/1 with no synergy on board
annotations.betterLine: Cast Rousing Read targeting Blood Artist to immediately draw 2 cards (discard 1), create a flying blocker/threat, and dig for answers while at 11 life facing two 3/3s

annotations.description: Cast Time to Feed before playing Forest from hand. Playing the land first is strictly better sequencing - it doesn't change available mana for this spell but ensures the land drop isn't accidentally missed and keeps options open.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Time to Feed before playing Forest land drop
annotations.betterLine: Play Forest first, then cast Time to Feed. Land drops should come before spells when there's no reason to delay them.

annotations.description: Blood Artist's death trigger requires choosing a target player who loses 1 life while the controller gains 1 life. QwCdr Folksy targeted themselves, meaning they lose 1 life and gain 1 life (net zero), instead of targeting the opponent for a 2-life swing (opponent loses 1, they gain 1). At 11 life against a 20 life opponent, every point matters.
annotations.actionTaken: Targeted themselves with Blood Artist's trigger, netting 0 life change.
annotations.betterLine: Target GPT53C Trash with Blood Artist's trigger so the opponent loses 1 life and you gain 1 life, a 2-point life swing in your favor.

annotations.description: At 5 life with 5 mana available, the player cast only Erratic Visionary (2 mana) instead of casting Rousing Read on Silversmote Ghoul first (3 mana, making it a 4/2 flyer and drawing 2 cards) and then casting Erratic Visionary with the remaining 2 mana. This missed both significant card advantage (draw 2) and creating a 4/2 flying threat that could attack over the opponent's ground creatures while the opponent's board was tapped.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Erratic Visionary for {1}{U}, leaving 3 mana unused and missing the opportunity to also cast Rousing Read.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Rousing Read on Silversmote Ghoul first ({2}{U}), drawing 2 cards and creating a 4/2 flyer, then cast Erratic Visionary with the remaining {1}{U}. This maximizes mana usage, card advantage, and creates a flying clock while the opponent has no flyers and Crushing Canopy is in the graveyard.

annotations.description: At 5 life against an opponent at 23, casting Library Larcenist instead of Rousing Read on Silversmote Ghoul misses immediate card advantage and a flying threat. Rousing Read draws 2 cards immediately (discard 1), makes Silversmote Ghoul a 4/2 flyer that can attack over ground creatures, and still leaves 2 mana for Erratic Visionary. Library Larcenist is a 1/2 that needs to survive and attack to draw, which is far too slow at 5 life.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Library Larcenist (1/2 ground creature with conditional draw)
annotations.betterLine: Cast Rousing Read targeting Silversmote Ghoul to immediately draw 2 cards (discard 1), create a 4/2 flyer, then cast Erratic Visionary with remaining mana. This provides both immediate card selection to find answers and a meaningful evasive clock.

annotations.description: At 5 life facing lethal next turn from opponent's 3/3s, the player failed to deploy any of the three castable spells in hand (Erratic Visionary at 1U, Library Larcenist at 2U, or Rousing Read at 2U) and also failed to successfully activate Silversmote Ghoul's sacrifice-to-draw ability despite having sufficient mana (2 Swamps + 3 Islands). Deploying blockers like Erratic Visionary and Library Larcenist would help survive the next attack, and Rousing Read on Silversmote Ghoul could provide a flying blocker plus card draw.
annotations.actionTaken: Attempted to activate Silversmote Ghoul but failed mana payment; passed without casting any spells, ending the turn with 5 unspent mana and 3 castable cards in hand.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Library Larcenist (2U) and Erratic Visionary (1U) to deploy two blockers, using all 5 available mana. Alternatively, cast one creature and hold mana for potential interaction, but deploying blockers at 5 life is critical.

annotations.description: At 5 life facing lethal next turn (5/3 Trufflesnout + 3/3 Armorcraft Judge = 8 damage), QwCdr declined to sacrifice the tapped Silversmote Ghoul to draw a card. The Ghoul being tapped means it can't block this turn. Even if it untaps, blocking the 3/3 Judge still leaves the 5/3 Trufflesnout dealing exactly lethal. Drawing a card here could find removal or another answer to survive.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed on activating Silversmote Ghoul's sacrifice ability to draw a card.
annotations.betterLine: Sacrifice Silversmote Ghoul ({1}{B}) to draw a card, hoping to find removal like another Last Gasp or a bounce spell to survive the lethal attack. Still have 3 Islands left to cast Erratic Visionary or Library Larcenist afterward.

annotations.description: Opponent is at 5 life with only a tapped Silversmote Ghoul as a blocker. GPT53C has Trufflesnout (5/3) and Armorcraft Judge (3/3) for 8 total power - attacking with both is lethal since the Ghoul is tapped and can't block. Instead, the player passed priority in precombat main with nothing on the stack, ending their turn and missing a lethal attack.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority in precombat main phase, effectively ending the turn without attacking, playing a land, or casting any spells.
annotations.betterLine: Play Forest, optionally cast Fertilid for an additional attacker, then go to combat and attack with Trufflesnout and Armorcraft Judge for 8 damage against an opponent at 5 life with no untapped blockers - this is lethal.

annotations.description: QwCdr Folksy is at 5 life facing 8 damage (Trufflesnout 5/3 + Armorcraft Judge 3/3) with no untapped blockers. Silversmote Ghoul is tapped and cannot block, so sacrificing it to draw a card is the only possible out to find an answer (like another Last Gasp to kill the 5/3 Trufflesnout, reducing damage to 3 and surviving at 2 life). Without drawing, they die to this attack with certainty.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without activating Silversmote Ghoul's sacrifice-to-draw ability.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Silversmote Ghoul's {1}{B} sacrifice ability to draw a card, hoping to find an instant-speed answer like a removal spell to survive the lethal attack.

annotations.description: Player declined to sacrifice Silversmote Ghoul to draw a card while facing lethal combat damage (8 damage vs 5 life). The Ghoul is tapped and can't block, so sacrificing it costs nothing. Drawing a card gives a small chance of finding an instant-speed answer.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without activating Silversmote Ghoul's sacrifice-to-draw ability.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Silversmote Ghoul's '{1}{B}, Sacrifice: Draw a card' ability. Even though the odds of finding a relevant instant are low, it's a free draw with no downside since the Ghoul can't block and the player is dying regardless.
